paper_title: Recent Progress in All-Solution-Processed Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What is the record power conversion efficiency (PCE) for all-solution-processed organic solar cells mentioned in the literature, and what materials were used to achieve it?
qa_pairs.answer: The highest reported PCE for an all-solution-processed organic solar cell is 15.26%. This was achieved in a small-area device (0.041 cm²) using a PM6:PC71BM:BTP-eC9 active layer blend, an alcohol-dispersed conducting polymer complex, and a spray-coated silver nanowire (AgNW) top electrode.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in All-Solution-Processed Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How can the surface roughness of silver nanowire (AgNW) electrodes be reduced to improve device fabrication?
qa_pairs.answer: The surface roughness of AgNW electrodes can be significantly reduced from approximately 11 nm to 5 nm by wrapping the nanowires with aluminum-doped ZnO (AZO). This process effectively fills the gaps and holes between the AgNWs, creating a smoother surface for subsequent layer deposition.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in All-Solution-Processed Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What modification to the PEDOT:PSS formulation was developed to resolve wetting issues with non-fullerene acceptors, and why is it effective?
qa_pairs.answer: The PSS counter ion in PEDOT:PSS was replaced with perfluorinated sulfonic acid (PFSA) to create a material known as PEDOT:F. This modification is effective because PEDOT:F is alcohol/water-soluble, which overcomes the wetting issues that conventional water-only dispersed PEDOT:PSS faces when applied over non-fullerene acceptors.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in All-Solution-Processed Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Explain the dual advantages of using hydrogen molybdenum bronze (HxMoO3) as a hole transport layer (HTL) in all-solution-processed devices.
qa_pairs.answer: HxMoO3 serves as an effective HTL because it possesses a deep Fermi level of -5.44 eV, which facilitates efficient hole extraction. Additionally, it is processed using ethanol and exhibits good wettability, which helps solve the interface wetting problems commonly found between non-fullerene acceptors and traditional PEDOT:PSS layers.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in All-Solution-Processed Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What strategy can be employed to enhance the conductivity of PEDOT:PSS electrodes to as high as 4200 S/cm?
qa_pairs.answer: A layer-by-layer (LBL) co-doping strategy can be used, involving the superimposition of two PEDOT:PSS thin layers that are gradually treated with sulfuric acid and ethylene glycol (EG). This treatment removes the insulating PSS components, leading to a maximum conductivity of 4200 S/cm.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in All-Solution-Processed Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the hot pressing technique contribute to both the electronic and mechanical stability of AgNW/PEDOT:PSS composite electrodes?
qa_pairs.answer: Hot pressing firmly integrates AgNWs into the PEDOT:PSS film, reducing electrode roughness and preventing device failure caused by protruding nanowires that might otherwise cause shorts. Mechanically, this integration significantly improves the bending performance of the devices, making them more durable for flexible applications.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in All-Solution-Processed Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What are the performance metrics and structural benefits of using a 'ferroconcrete-like' AZO@AgNWs@AZO (AAA) composite electrode in semi-transparent organic solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The AAA composite electrode provides 3D long-range pathways for efficient charge transfer and collection. Using this architecture, semi-transparent organic solar cells have achieved a power conversion efficiency of 10.90% and an average visible transmittance (AVT) of 26.64%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in All-Solution-Processed Organic Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What level of long-term stability have all-solution-processed OSCs demonstrated when using transfer-printed PEDOT:PSS electrodes?
qa_pairs.answer: Devices utilizing transfer-printed PEDOT:PSS electrodes co-doped with acid and ethylene glycol have shown excellent shelf-life stability, retaining approximately 91% of their initial power conversion efficiency (PCE) after 300 days of storage in an inert gas atmosphere.
qa_pairs.source_title: Recent Progress in All-Solution-Processed Organic Solar Cells
